title: Can $π$ generate itself? A Monte Carlo analysis of 314 trillion digits
summary: At the end of 2025, a record computation of $π$ reached 314 trillion decimal digits, providing the largest numerical dataset ever generated for this constant. We exploit this unprecedented dataset to investigate whether the digits of $π$ themselves can serve as a source of pseudorandom numbers for estimating $π$ through the simplest Monte Carlo method. Our results go beyond the normality hypothesis by providing empirical evidence of a high degree of statistical randomness in the available digits, although not of digit independence, which cannot hold for a deterministic sequence.
